outcome: infant mortality due to congenital anomalies
cohort: The study included 2199 women from health centers in nine provinces of Iran, divided into a group of mothers whose infants died due to congenital anomalies and a control group of mothers with live births or infant deaths due to other causes.
finding: History of cesarean delivery, maternal age, area of living, maternal smoking during pregnancy, consanguineous marriage, and birth weight < 2500g were significantly associated with infant death due to congenital anomalies.
mod_finding: A history of cesarean delivery was significantly associated with infant death due to congenital anomalies (OR: 2.09).
birth_weight: Birth weight < 2500g was identified as a significant factor.
